subject: Bounded WVB typed-directory decoding and fast current-source development tests
claim: Twenty-four WV component case groups pass against the actual verifier directory module, including exact five-byte cells, distinct immutable payload identities, 8,192 slots, malformed/truncated shapes, checked ranges, E1 instruction boundaries, and branch predecessors. The warm owner ran fresh behavior in 1,266 ms. This is a component checkpoint, not complete WVB 1.39 admission.

source.value: Worktree based on cbc6a28e56a3e045374d59cfe7119a693ce07e0e; exact final component and runner inputs below. Initial three-case measurements used cases 1 through 3 of the subsequently expanded fixture, before control-directory bounds and E1 cases were added. The deliberate identity mutation was restored before warm validation.

limitations: The complete metadata/semantic verifier, typed operand-stack and lifetime checks, and all execution consumers still reject candidate WVB 1.39. The internal 64-plus-payload-kind cell representation is not a serialized shape or permission to execute a module.

Directory decoding does not prove version eligibility, nominal declarations, canonical Option/Result relationships, value availability, owner freezing, call confinement, branch lifetime agreement, or non-escape. Those remain complete-verifier work.

The existing memory-budget owner has 234 declared cases after these additions, and the combined publication selector has 63. Neither complete selection was rerun here. Prior publication evidence is separate and unchanged.

The all-changed-file plan proposed nine owners and 2,550 expected seconds. It was not executed under the ten-minute development budget; current component behavior and routing were checked with the exact focused owner.

Measurements are single local observations in an existing bootstrap cache, not clean-host benchmarks, speedup thresholds, Linux reproduction, complete qualification, or peak-memory evidence. No process-tree peak working set was captured.
The pure WV fixture currently uses the bootstrap source syntax; edition-1 migration remains within the overall migration goal.

Two temporary fixture syntax errors and one dependency ordinal-order error were corrected before their relevant final passes. No failed development attempt is counted as passing complete verification.
